summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Edward F. Wente, an American Egyptologist and professor emeritus at the University of Chicago's Department of Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations. It covers his birth year, his doctorate and lecturing years at Chicago, and his membership in the Oriental Institute. It also names one of his major works, Letters from Ancient Egypt (1990), and a 1999 Festschrift of Egyptological essays published in his honor.
one_line: Biographical note on Edward F. Wente, American Egyptologist and emeritus professor at the University of Chicago, with his major works and a 1999 honorary volume.
key_facts: Edward Frank Wente was born in 1930.
Edward F. Wente is an American professor emeritus of Egyptology.
Edward F. Wente is professor emeritus in the Department of Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations at the University of Chicago.
Edward F. Wente received his Ph.D from the University of Chicago in 1959.
Edward F. Wente lectured at the University of Chicago from 1963 to 1996.
Edward F. Wente is a longstanding member of the Oriental Institute, Chicago.
Letters from Ancient Egypt (1990) is one of Edward F. Wente's major works.
Letters from Ancient Egypt was published by the Scholarly Press.
In 1999 the Oriental Institute published Gold of Praise: Studies on Ancient Egypt in Honor of Edward F. Wente.
Gold of Praise is a collection of essays by Egyptologists honoring Edward Wente.
